assertion.en: If the frequency of a sound wave in air is doubled, the speed of the sound is doubled too.

reason.en: In the same medium the speed of sound stays the same, so doubling the frequency halves the wavelength.

optionFeedback.a: Check the Assertion again: does a higher frequency make sound travel faster in the same air?
optionFeedback.b: Check the Assertion again: the speed of sound in air does not depend on the frequency.
optionFeedback.c: It is the other way round. The Reason is true; check the Assertion again.

explanation.en: The Assertion is false and the Reason is true. In the same air, sound travels at the same speed whatever its frequency. Since v = λ × ν, if ν doubles and v stays the same, λ is halved.

hints.en: First decide whether each statement is true on its own.
Does the speed of sound in air depend on the source, or on the air?
